llm_response.content:
Empirical Research Plan:  Clean Air Act (1970) → Air Quality → Adult Mortality, 1968–1978  

--------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
Strategy: Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed effects) complemented by an event-study and a 2SLS robustness exercise that instruments actual pollution with policy-driven “non-attainment” status.  

Why appropriate:  
• Clean Air Act set statutory concentration ceilings (NAAQS) for six criteria pollutants.  In 1971 EPA classified each county‐pollutant pair as “non-attainment” (above standard) or “attainment” (below).  
• Only non-attainment counties were legally required to adopt abatement plans and faced compliance deadlines (1975 for particulates).  
• Hence, the Act generated a plausibly exogenous, differential reduction in pollution across space and time—ideal for DID.  
• Panel data (1968–1978) allow observation of outcomes before and after treatment for both treated and control counties.  
• Event‐study permits visual and statistical assessment of the parallel-trend assumption.  
• Because pollution changes are endogenous (firms may locate differently, people migrate), a policy-induced dummy can serve as an instrument in a 2SLS robustness specification (Chay-Greenstone style).  

--------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control  
Treatment variable  
TREATc = 1 if county c was classified by EPA in 1971 as “non-attainment” for Total Suspended Particulates (TSP) or PM, 0 otherwise.  
(Alternative: intensity measure = initial exceedance above the NAAQS in 1970, used in a continuous-treatment DID.)  

Treatment timing / event date  
Event year = 1971 (designation).  Abatement expected to phase-in 1971–75.  For estimation we code POSTt = 1 for 1972–1978 and 0 for 1968–1970.  Event-study uses individual year dummies.  

Control group  
“All other counties” that were in attainment for particulates (TREAT=0).  They faced no binding requirement, so serve as counterfactual for mortality trends absent mandated clean-up.  Control counties in the same state are preferable (state×year FE absorb state-level shocks).  

Instrument (for robustness)  
Zc = non-attainment status × POSTt – interacts with post indicator to generate exogenous variation in measured pollution.  

Running variable / cutoff  
Not applicable (no RDD).  

--------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1 Parallel trends: In absence of the Act, adult mortality trends in attainment and non-attainment counties would have evolved similarly.  Plausibility: both sets were subject to the same national health environment; pre-1971 trends can be inspected.  

A2 No differential contemporaneous shocks: No other policy between 1971–78 differentially affected non-attainment counties.  Plausibility: Medicare (1965) and OSHA (1970) were nationwide; still, economic downturns tied to manufacturing might correlate with non-attainment, so controls for county economic structure are added.  

A3 Stable composition & no selective migration that is itself health-related.  Plausibility: Migration likely modest over 3–5 years; we will test by checking population size/age structure stability.  

A4 SUTVA / no cross-county spillovers: Abatement in non-attainment counties does not meaningfully change air quality in nearby attainment counties (wind patterns minimal at county averages).  We will test by dropping counties within 50 km of a treated county.  

A5 Accurate classification: Non-attainment status is assigned mechanically by measured 1970 TSP > NAAQS; unlikely to anticipate mortality changes.   

--------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies  

T1 Baseline differences or divergent pre-trends.  
 Remedy:  i) Event-study; ii) county-level linear pre-trend controls; iii) matching: restrict controls to counties with similar 1968–1970 mortality and socio-economic levels.  

T2 Economic shocks correlated with pollution cuts (e.g., plant closures).  
 Remedy:  i) Include county×industry employment shares interacted with year; ii) control for unemployment, income per capita; iii) IV for pollution with non-attainment × post so the effect is identified off regulation-driven rather than demand-driven changes.  

T3 Migration / composition bias.  
 Remedy:  i) Control for age-specific population counts; ii) run specifications on age-adjusted mortality rates; iii) placebo test on short-run population inflows.  

--------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline  

```r
# Required packages
library(fixest)      # fast fe estimators
library(tidyverse)   # data manipulation
library(haven)       # if Stata dta files also present

# 1. Load data -----------------------------------------------------------
mort  <- read_csv("county_mortality_1968_1978.csv")   # county, year, deaths, pop
poll  <- read_csv("county_pollution_1968_1978.csv")   # county, year, pm
status<- read_csv("nonattainment_status_1971.csv")    # county, nonattain_dummy

# 2. Merge & construct variables ----------------------------------------
df <- mort %>%
      left_join(poll,   by = c("county","year")) %>%
      left_join(status, by = "county") %>%
      mutate(adult_mort   = deaths_adult / pop_adult * 100000,
             treat        = nonattain_dummy,          # 1 = treated
             post         = if_else(year >= 1972, 1,0),
             treat_post   = treat*post,
             year_factor  = factor(year))

# Optional continuous treatment
# df <- df %>% mutate(treat_intensity = pm1970 - 75)  # 75 µg/m3 = NAAQS TSP

# 3. Main DID specification ---------------------------------------------
did_spec <- feols(adult_mort ~ treat*post | county + year, data = df,
                  weights = ~pop_adult, cluster = ~state)
summary(did_spec)

# 4. Event-study --------------------------------------------------------
event_spec <- feols(adult_mort ~ i(year, treat, ref = 1970) | county + year,
                    data = df, weights = ~pop_adult, cluster = ~state)
iplot(event_spec)          # visualize leads/lags

# 5. IV robustness: policy→pollution→mortality --------------------------
# first stage: pollution
fs <- feols(pm ~ treat*post | county + year, data = df, cluster = ~state)

# second stage via 2SLS
iv_spec <- feols(adult_mort ~ 1 | county + year | pm ~ treat*post,
                 data = df, cluster = ~state, weights = ~pop_adult)
summary(iv_spec)

# 6. Additional robustness: exclude counties within 50 km --------------
border <- read_csv("county_border_distance.csv")      # distance to nearest treated
df_rb <- df %>% filter(distance_treated >= 50)

did_rb <- feols(adult_mort ~ treat*post | county + year, data = df_rb,
                cluster = ~state, weights = ~pop_adult)
summary(did_rb)
```

--------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results (Prior)  

Sign: A reduction in particulate matter should decrease adult (age 25–64) mortality.  Epidemiological estimates suggest an elasticity of roughly –0.10 to –0.20: a 10 µg/m³ decline in TSP could lower adult mortality by ~1–2%.  Non-attainment counties experienced ≈15–20 µg/m³ declines, so an expected 2–4% drop in adult mortality relative to controls (≈3–7 deaths per 100 000).  

--------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
C1 Parallel pre-trends visually/statistically supported……………… 0.8  
C2 No simultaneous confounding policies………………………………… 0.6  
C3 Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers)………………………… 0.7  
C4 Correct functional form / weighting…………………………………… 0.9  
C5 Robustness across specifications / samples………………………… 0.9  

Overall: cautiously credible but hinges on demonstrated pre-trend balance and spillover tests.
